A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REASONING COMPILER study. All 27 pages in each version, including equations, figures, Tables 1–8, Appendices A–G, and the checklist, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original compiler performance and sample-efficiency measurements, ablations, API costs, and proposal fallback rates.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices B–G.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the UCT exploitation term 1/(κN) with W/N and introduces sign-adjusted rollout rewards and reward backpropagation. This revises the stated search rule within the retained LLM–MCTS framework; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five kernels from Llama-3-8B, DeepSeek-R1, FLUX, and Llama-4-Scout, plus end-to-end Llama-3-8B, across the same five hardware platforms.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain TVM MetaSchedule with evolutionary search and unguided MCTS. The LLM alternatives also remain unchanged. REASONING COMPILER replaces labels such as MCTS + LLM without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported hardware, TVM version, proposal models, exploration parameter, branching factors, sample budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Deleting the noise-control sentence removes documentation without establishing a changed measurement procedure.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices C–G retain the same model-choice, historical-context, branching-factor, and proposal-validity analyses. Their experimental questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated 20 times and report mean performance. Neither adds seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 match, and the plotted results in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. The reported layer-wise and end-to-end sample-efficiency gains remain 10.8× and 5.6×, respectively.

T1.justification: Section 2 changes the reward definition from f(a(p)) to s·f(a(p)), with s chosen to make larger rewards preferable. Section 3.2 revises the cumulative-reward definition and UCT equation. These are mathematical corrections; the existing assumptions and asymptotic-optimality argument remain unchanged, with no new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution: combining contextual LLM proposals with MCTS, without retraining, to improve compiler sample efficiency. The headline empirical claims and their scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning contextual reasoning, operator structure, model capability, and historical depth are retained. The checklist preserves the same limitations concerning external APIs, restricted benchmark coverage, model variability, and context constraints.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from Anna-Bele/LLM_MCTS_Search to he-actlab/REASONING_COMPILER. Section 4.1 removes the statement about disabling background processes and avoiding competing workloads. Other implementation and resource disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The same cited sources and substantive novelty contrasts are retained. Browne et al.'s MCTS survey moves from reference 20 to reference 9 and receives earlier citations; bibliographic corrections and the Section 5 rewrite do not materially change research positioning.

P1.justification: v5 standardizes method and workload terminology, edits sentences, and renames Section 4 and its subsections to Evaluation, Methodology, and Experimental Results. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive revised performance/reward labels, tables receive heading and typography adjustments, and Appendix A gains shaded prompt and response boxes. Captions and text placement change locally; all figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 improves the mathematical specification through the UCT correction and explicit reward orientation, while clearer naming and boxed prompt examples improve presentation. The gains are limited: empirical evidence is unchanged, the sign convention is not fully reflected in Equation 1 and Figure 2, and the measurement-noise disclosure is removed.
